subject.title: Bound batch file read with size cap in config-set-input

question: What public capacity and failure contract should `openclaw config set --batch-file` guarantee for already-valid large batch files?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but choosing a new hard rejection threshold changes an existing CLI input contract and cannot be inferred from boundary tests or an adjacent metadata-reader limit.

options.title: Approve an 8 MiB batch-file contract
options.body: Keep this cap, document the intentional upgrade behavior and supported recovery path, and retain exact-boundary coverage.

options.title: Choose a compatible capacity contract
options.body: Set the cap from an agreed config/batch payload contract and add focused regression coverage for the selected limit and failure behavior.

options.title: Defer the hard cap
options.body: Keep the existing input behavior while a separately approved bounded or streaming parsing design is defined.

recommendation.title: Choose a compatible capacity contract
recommendation.body: Set the cap from an agreed config/batch payload contract and add focused regression coverage for the selected limit and failure behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent merged bounded-read pattern and are the strongest available history-based routing candidate for the primitive and its limit rationale.
